newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Swire sets US$300 mln perpetual bond.
newsitem.headline: Swire sets US$300 mln perpetual bond.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said on Thursday that Swire Pacific Ltd had completed the first perpetual bond offering by an Asian issuer, raising a total of US$300 million.

The bonds have a coupon of 9.33 percent and the issuer has the right to call them back from bondholders at par after 10 years and thereafter annually. Otherwise, the bonds will not mature. The bonds will be listed on the Luxembourg Stock exchange.

The issue was placed on a global basis with about 50 percent being placed with investors in Asia, 10 percent in Europe and 40 percent in the United States. The issue size was increased from US$150 million to US$300 million as a result of increased demand.

Undated or perpetual debt ranks lower than senior debt on a Hong Kong company's balance sheet, but senior to equity. Consequently, the issue has been rated A- by Standard and Poor's and Baa1 by Moody's Investors Service Inc. These ratings are one grade below senior debt ratings.
From Swire Pacific's point of view this issue of perpetual debt represents a cheaper and more tax efficient method of raising new capital than a new equity rights issue, Merrill said.

Swire Pacific Ltd is the holding company of a Hong Kong based conglomerate that engages in a wide range of businesses, primarily in Asia, including aviation, property investment and development, soft drink bottling, manufacturing, retailing, marine services and insurance.
